note.question: How should intensively a firm use emotion-AI signals to allocate resources when customers can manipulate their emotional expressions?
note.overview: The firm commits to an emotion-contingent allocation rule while privately typed users strategically distort expressed emotion; the paper explicitly solves the resulting Stackelberg equilibrium.

components.label: Stackelberg equilibrium between a committing firm and a strategic user
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Stackelberg equilibrium between a committing firm and a strategic user. Equation (3), printed p. 633 (PDF p. 7), gives the user's best response x*=eta+(s/2)beta gamma. The firm then minimizes expected misallocation and spillover loss anticipating this response; the formal equilibrium and Lemmas 1-2 appear on printed p. 635 (PDF p. 9).

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The firm commits to a linear allocation rule. A user observes her natural emotion and gaming ability, chooses an expressed emotion, the AI observes the expression with noise, and the firm applies the committed allocation. A two-dimensional user type creates heterogeneous natural signals and manipulation costs. The allocation slope both uses information and creates an incentive to game.
